input.axialHint: The calculation uses N only for the N–M check of the cross-section, not for second-order effects.
input.boredPile: Cast in place (minimum reinforcement bored pile)
input.coverTitle: Distance from the concrete edge to the bar centre
input.designValues: H, M and N are design values.
input.eiHint: EI = Ec,eff·Ic + Es·Is + Ea·Ia with Ec,eff = Ec × project factor / (1 + creep). Enter design strengths including material factors.
input.gradeHint: The selection lists fill in fck and fcd = fck / 1.5, fyd = fyk / 1.15 and fy / 1.0; a custom value remains possible.
input.head: Pile head
input.headAssumed: Pile head assumed at NAP 0.00; enter the actual level.
input.k0Hint: k₀ = kh × effective width. Between layers without subgrade reaction the soil provides no support.
input.momentHint: Sign of M: a positive moment turns the pile head anticlockwise and counteracts a positive H. A force H at height e above the head gives M = −H·e.
input.puHint: pu(z) = min(pu,max; pu,0 + g·z), ultimate resistance per metre of pile.
input.retainingHint: Retaining model: Δp = Ka·q with Ka = tan²(45° − φ/2), line load = Δp × influence width. Only the increase due to q; no strip load or soil movement around a free pile.
input.sheetHint: I, W and A come from the section library, per m of continuous wall. Per m of wall, H, M and N apply per running metre and the soil springs act over 1.00 m. A single pile is calculated over the pile width, like a narrow pile. β_B (on W) and β_D (on I) reduce the values if the interlocks do not transfer shear: 1.0 for Z-sections and for U-sections with fixed interlocks; lower for single or non-fixed U-piles, according to the national annex of NEN-EN 1993-5. This is not a sheet pile wall calculation: no earth pressure on both sides, anchorage or staging.
input.sheetMaterialHint: The yield strength follows from the selected steel grade in the library; γ_M0 = 1.0.
input.sheetSpringHint: Continuous wall: effective width 1.00 m, without lateral spread. Single pile: the pile width, as for a pile.
input.timberNote: {{name}}: the lateral calculation has no cross-section check for timber yet.
input.wallTitle: Effective residual wall thickness after corrosion
input.openTubeHint: Open tube: calculated as a hollow tube; the soil inside does not add stiffness. The inner face is also in contact with soil.
input.menardTitle: k_h from E_p (Ménard, CUR 166) at the working width
input.puKindTitle: pu as a profile or after Brinch Hansen
input.bhHint: BH: pu(z) = K_q(z)·γ′·z·D after Brinch Hansen (1961), z from the soil surface (with water from the bed), γ′ under water = γ_sat − 10.
input.menardHint: Ménard: k_h from the pressuremeter modulus E_p and α (CUR 166).

notes.boredDetail: Art. 9.8.5 (4): at least 6 bars of at least Ø16; the clear bar spacing of at most 200 mm is not checked.
notes.class3: Cross-section class 3: checked elastically. The N–M curve and the u.c. of the N–M cross-section check above are plastic and do not apply to this tube.
notes.class4: Cross-section class 4: local buckling governs. That is outside the scope of this check (NEN-EN 1993-1-6); the resistances are not calculated.
notes.class4Short: Outside the scope of this check (cross-section class 4).
notes.compositeDelta: δ outside 0.2 to 0.9: for δ < 0.2 check as reinforced concrete, for δ > 0.9 as steel.
notes.compositeDt: D/t above the limit: local buckling may not be neglected; outside the simplified method.
notes.compositeMethod: Steel-concrete cross-section according to the simplified method: fully plastic stress blocks, concrete tension neglected, no increase due to confinement. Composite action is demonstrated according to the input.
notes.compositeScope: Outside the scope: the method applies to S235 up to and including S460, C20/25 up to and including C50/60 and longitudinal reinforcement up to 6 % of the concrete area.
notes.cotRange: cot θ must lie between 1.0 and 2.5 (art. 6.2.3 (2)).
notes.crackNA: Not possible: the module has one load case, which is checked as a design value. The crack width requires a quasi-permanent or frequent combination; that is not part of the input.
notes.designValues: The internal forces from the entered load case are taken as design values in the ultimate limit state; N_Ed is the axial force at the head over the whole pile.
notes.hoopFactor: Circular stirrups or spiral: π/4 of the bar force acts in the shear direction (Priestley, Seible & Calvi 1996); the standard does not give that factor.
notes.noBars: No longitudinal reinforcement: art. 6.2.2 applies to reinforced concrete. Plain concrete (chapter 12) is not included.
notes.notComposite: Not checked: shear connection and load introduction between tube and concrete (art. 6.7.4), member buckling (art. 6.7.3.5; the pile is supported by the soil), second-order effects, creep and shrinkage in the strength, crack width and corrosion (enter the residual wall thickness). The increase due to confinement is not used.
notes.notConcrete: Not checked: crack width, anchorage and lap splices, detailing of stirrups in columns (art. 9.5.3), concrete cover and durability, buckling and second-order effects (P–Δ), a cracked bending stiffness, fatigue, and for precast piles transport, lifting and driving.
notes.notSheet: Not checked: shear buckling of the web (the web angle is not in the library), buckling (art. 5.2.3), cross-section class 4, the interlocks, anchorage and walings, local load introduction, fatigue and corrosion. The earth pressure on both sides of a wall belongs to a sheet pile wall calculation.
notes.notTube: Not checked: member buckling (art. 6.3; the pile is supported by the soil), cross-section class 4 and shell buckling (NEN-EN 1993-1-6), second-order effects (P–Δ), welds and connections, fatigue and corrosion (enter the residual wall thickness).
notes.roundShear: Circular cross-section: b_w and d according to the usual substitution (Clarke & Birjandi 1993; Feltham 2004); the standard does not give it.
notes.sheetBeta: Reduced for shear transfer in the interlocks: β_B = {{bb}} on the section modulus, β_D = {{bd}} on the bending stiffness.
notes.sheetClass4: Cross-section class 4 for {{grade}} according to the catalogue: local buckling governs. That is outside the scope of this check (NEN-EN 1993-5 annex A); the resistances are not calculated.
notes.sheetClassIs: Class {{cls}} for {{grade}} according to the manufacturer's catalogue.
notes.sheetModel: The section is a beam on soil springs over a calculation width of {{b}} m; H, M and N apply over that width. This is not a sheet pile wall calculation: no active and passive earth pressure on both sides, no anchorage and no staging.
notes.sheetNoClass: The library gives no cross-section class for this section for {{grade}}: calculated elastically. Verify yourself that the cross-section is not class 4.
notes.sheetNoWeb: Not possible: the web thickness, height or flange thickness of this section is not in the library.
notes.sheetNoWpl: The library gives no plastic section modulus: calculated elastically.
notes.sheetSingle: Single pile: the library gives I, W and A per m of continuous wall. A single U-pile has its own neutral axis and therefore a smaller I and W; account for that with β_B and β_D or with the manufacturer's values.
notes.stirrupsNotNeeded: V_Ed ≤ V_Rd,c: no shear reinforcement is required by calculation; the rules for the stirrups are shown for information.
notes.strainComposite: Existing check with plane sections and concrete compressive strain 3.5 ‰; stricter than the plastic method of NEN-EN 1994-1-1 below.
notes.strainMethod: M_Rd at N_Ed from the strain diagram: parabola-rectangle, concrete compressive strain 3.5 ‰, concrete tension neglected.
notes.tubeIgnored: According to the input the tube does not contribute: the concrete core with its reinforcement is checked, without the tube.
notes.tubeYield: f_y is the entered design value f_yd of the tube steel times γ_M0 = 1.0; the wall thickness is the entered residual wall thickness.
notes.corrosionTube: Checked with the section after corrosion, including the section class and D/t. {{stiffness}}
notes.corrosionSheet: Checked with the profile after corrosion ({{basis}}), with the section class at the reduced flange thickness. {{stiffness}}

Thickness loss per side; the table values are the recommended values of NEN-EN 1993-5 tables 4-1 and 4-2 and have not been checked against the code text or the Dutch annex. Corrosion counts in the material check and the N–M check, including the section class and D/t; in the force distribution only with the tick box. A filled tube only corrodes on the outside.

water.hint: No soil springs between pile head and water bed (free length {{free}} m). The soil starts at the bed; the effective stress (Brinch Hansen) counts from the bed with γ′, without surcharge from the water.
water.formula: q = ½·ρ·C_D·D·u² per metre, from the bed to the water level; design value γ·q, like H. C_D depends on the Reynolds number, roughness and marine growth: enter a justified value (there is no default). Not included: wave loading (Morison, inertia term) and dynamic effects (vortex shedding).
